name: rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations
what_it_holds: Committed CSVs analyzing San Francisco housing vs. short-term rentals: SF City Performance Scorecard hotel-rate data (Jul 2004-May 2018), Zillow long-term rental rates (Nov 2010-Sep 2018), DataSF home-price/assessment data (2007-2016, not uploaded due to GitHub size limits, downloadable from DataSF instead), and Inside Airbnb peer-to-peer short-term-rental rates (May 2015-Dec 2017). No 311/complaints/enforcement data; explicitly notes only 3 data points exist for the STR series, limiting granularity.
why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023) for San Francisco with an 8-9 year old vintage we do not otherwise have on the CDN.

name: short-term-rentals-warehouse
what_it_holds: dbt/Snowflake data-warehouse project (create_warehouse.sql, extract.py, kaggle_data.py, listings.py, load.py) that stitches together Inside Airbnb listing data (CC0), a Kaggle world-cities-population dataset, and a Kaggle cost-of-living-index dataset into a star schema, described as covering 'over 35 million records from 2015-2020' across global cities, with Metabase dashboards on top. 68 commits, 2 open PRs. No committed CSV/parquet data files were visible in the directory listing seen (extract.py presumably pulls from Inside Airbnb's own CDN/URLs at run time) — since Inside Airbnb's CDN no longer serves 2015-2020 vintages, re-running this pipeline today would likely NOT reproduce the historical 2015-2020 coverage the README claims unless the author's original run captured URLs that are since gone.
why_useful: If the extract.py source URLs or any cached intermediate files still resolve to older Inside Airbnb dump snapshots (worth a follow-up check), this could be a lead on gap #1 (pre-2023 Inside Airbnb dumps archived somewhere). As-is it is a pipeline definition, not a data cache, so treat as medium-low until verified whether it holds/points to actual archived dumps.

name: pyairbnb (johnbalvin)
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python client (149 stars, updated 8 Sep 2026 -- actively maintained) wrapping Airbnb's internal search/PDP APIs, no login needed. Functions: search_all()/search_all_from_url() (listings with price, availability dates, reviews count/rating, host details, amenities, cancellation policy), get_details() (per-listing prices/available dates/reviews/host), get_price() (nightly price for a given check-in/check-out), get_calendar() (month-level availability/price calendar per listing), get_reviews() (review text+metadata), get_listings_from_user()/get_host_details() (host's other listings), experience_search()/experience_search_by_place_id() (Airbnb Experiences), get_markets()/get_places_ids() (place-id lookup for city/region search boxes). Accepts lat/long bounding boxes for map search. No data committed -- code only.
why_useful: Most complete open client for exactly the fields the desk cannot get from Inside Airbnb after May 2025 (live nightly PRICE and CALENDAR availability by listing), which is gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy) and the 2026-calendar no-price gap noted in what-we-hold. Catalogue as METHOD ONLY -- running it against airbnb.com is the ToS decision CLAUDE.md reserves for a human; do not execute.
geography: global (any Airbnb market via search params)
themes: Airbnb API wrappers and search-page clients (catalogue only, never run): pyairbnb, airbnb-scraper, airbnb search results parsers; note what fields they expose
why_all: Most complete open client for exactly the fields the desk cannot get from Inside Airbnb after May 2025 (live nightly PRICE and CALENDAR availability by listing), which is gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy) and the 2026-calendar no-price gap noted in what-we-hold. Most actively maintained, highest-star pure-Python Airbnb client found. If a human decides scraping Airbnb search/calendar pages is in scope, this is the reference implementation for pulling nightly price and calendar-availability fields at scale (relevant to gap #2, realised ADR/occupancy) and for search-result counts as a nights/supply proxy. Method only, not data.

name: airbnbapi (zxol)
what_it_holds: 227-star, 53-fork Node.js wrapper around Airbnb's private mobile-app API (MIT, 107 commits). Exposes: property search with filters, public+private listing detail, host summaries/active listings, public calendar/pricing AND private calendar management (reservations, blocked days, dynamic pricing per date), guest/host user info, messaging threads, review submission, and batch reservation retrieval (host-side, needs auth token).
why_useful: Highest-star Airbnb API client found in this sweep; documents the richest field set (including host-side reservation/calendar internals) of any repo surveyed, useful as a reference for what fields Airbnb's own app exposes even if never run — e.g. confirms per-date dynamic pricing and blocked-day calendar fields exist server-side, which bears on how realised ADR/occupancy could in principle be reconstructed (gap #2).

name: airbnb-scraper (omkarcloud)
what_it_holds: Recently active repo (updated ~22 days before scout date; 5 stars, 4 commits) providing an API-style scraper covering 67 country domains. Fields: listing type/capacity/bedrooms/beds/baths, live nightly rate with breakdown (base, discounts, fees), real-time availability for given dates, host profile (superhost status, response rate, years hosting), amenities by category, review ratings incl. category sub-scores (cleanliness, accuracy, etc.), coordinates/address/place IDs, photos with captions, house rules/cancellation policy/sleeping arrangements. Extensive sample JSON responses in the README (documentation examples, not a committed dataset).
why_useful: Most field-rich single-listing schema found in this sweep (includes category-level review sub-scores and full cancellation-policy text, relevant to the RNPL/cancellation-distribution gap #3 if reconstructable from cancellation-policy metadata) and is one of the most recently updated repos surveyed.
